newsitem.title: UK: Williams makes offer for Chubb.
newsitem.headline: Williams makes offer for Chubb.

text.p: British conglomerate Williams Holdings Plc on Friday launched a 1.3 billion pounds ($2.12 billion) recommended bid for alarms and locks group Chubb Security Plc.
Williams offered two new Williams shares and 704.12 pence in cash for every three Chubb shares.
Williams had its eyes on Chubb in 1992 when it bid for its parent company Racal in 1992 but its efforts were thwarted and Chubb was subsequently demerged from the group and floated separately.
Williams said in a statement that acquiring Chubb would establish it as a world leader in fire protection and security.

The conglomerate issued a profit estimate along with its offer terms, forecasting an 11 percent rise in pre-tax pre-exceptional profits for 1996 to 243 million pounds ($396.5 million) and an exceptional profit of 97 million pounds, up from 9.0 million previously.
It said it expects a final dividend of 9.25p net, making 15.05p for the full year. ($1=.6128 Pound)
